# Technical Design: YAML Validator Command **Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command **Version**: 1.0.0 **Created**: 2026-03-08 **Status**: Draft --- ## 1. Design Overview A lightweight CLI command that validates YAML files for syntactic correctness. The command accepts a file path argument, reads the file, runs it through a hand-written YAML syntax validator, and reports the result with appropriate exit codes. No new dependencies are introduced -- all logic is implemented using only Bun built-ins and TypeScript. ### High-Level Architecture ```mermaid graph LR CLI["CLI Entry Point
validate-yaml.ts"] -->|reads| FS["File System
Bun.file()"] CLI -->|calls| VAL["YAML Validator
yaml-validator.ts"] VAL -->|returns| RES["ValidationResult
{valid, errors}"] CLI -->|outputs| OUT["stdout / stderr"] CLI -->|sets| EXIT["process.exit(code)"] TEST["yaml-validator.test.ts"] -->|tests| VAL ``` ## 2. Architecture The feature follows the existing single-layer script architecture. It introduces two new source files that mirror the existing `index.ts` / `utils.ts` separation pattern: a CLI entry point and a pure utility module. ### Component Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "New Files" A["src/validate-yaml.ts
(CLI Entry Point)"] B["src/yaml-validator.ts
(Pure Validation Logic)"] C["src/yaml-validator.test.ts
(Unit Tests)"] end subgraph "Existing Files" D["package.json
(Script Entry)"] end A -->|imports validateYaml| B C -->|imports validateYaml| B D -->|"bun run src/validate-yaml.ts"| A ``` ### Component Descriptions | Component | Purpose | Pattern | |-----------|---------|---------| | `src/yaml-validator.ts` | Pure validation logic. Exports `validateYaml()` function that accepts a string and returns a structured result. | Mirrors `src/utils.ts` -- pure functions, no side effects | | `src/validate-yaml.ts` | CLI entry point. Handles argument parsing, file reading, output formatting, exit codes. | Mirrors `src/index.ts` -- script entry, uses `process.argv` | | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` | Unit tests for the validation function. | Mirrors `src/utils.test.ts` -- co-located, `describe`/`test`/`expect` | | `package.json` (modified) | Adds `validate-yaml` script entry. | Follows existing script naming pattern | ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 Data Model **ValidationResult** -- Return type of the core validation function: ```typescript interface ValidationError { /** 1-based line number where the error was detected */ line: number; /** Human-readable description of the syntax error */ message: string; } interface ValidationResult { /** Whether the YAML content is syntactically valid */ valid: boolean; /** List of syntax errors found (empty if valid) */ errors: ValidationError[]; } ``` ### 3.2 Core Validation Logic (`src/yaml-validator.ts`) **Exported function**: ```typescript export function validateYaml(content: string): ValidationResult ``` **Validation checks performed** (in order): | Check | Description | Example Invalid Input | |-------|-------------|----------------------| | Tab indentation | YAML spec forbids tabs for indentation | `\tkey: value` | | Unclosed quoted strings | Detect unmatched single or double quotes in scalar values | `key: "unclosed value` | | Mismatched flow indicators | Unbalanced `[]` or `{}` in flow-style collections | `items: [a, b, c` | | Invalid mapping syntax | Lines that appear to be key-value pairs but have structural issues | `key value` (missing colon separator) | | Inconsistent indentation | Child items with indentation that does not align to a consistent block level | Mixed 2-space and 3-space nesting | | Document marker validation | Ensure `---` and `...` document markers are used correctly | `-- -` (malformed marker) | **Design notes**: - The validator processes the input line-by-line for simplicity and clarity. - Comment lines (starting with `#` after optional whitespace) and blank lines are skipped. - The validator does NOT attempt full YAML spec compliance. It targets common, practical syntax errors that developers encounter. - Empty input and whitespace-only input are treated as valid (empty YAML document). ### 3.3 CLI Entry Point (`src/validate-yaml.ts`) **Flow**: ```mermaid graph TB START["Start"] --> ARGS["Read process.argv[2]"] ARGS -->|missing| USAGE["Print usage to stderr
Exit code 1"] ARGS -->|present| READ["Read file via Bun.file(path).text()"] READ -->|error| FILEERR["Print file error to stderr
Exit code 1"] READ -->|success| VALIDATE["Call validateYaml(content)"] VALIDATE -->|valid| SUCCESS["Print success to stdout
Exit code 0"] VALIDATE -->|invalid| FAIL["Print errors to stderr
Exit code 1"] ``` **Output format**: | Scenario | Stream | Message | |----------|--------|---------| | Valid YAML | stdout | `Valid YAML: ` | | Invalid YAML | stderr | `Invalid YAML: \n Line : ` (one line per error) | | File not found | stderr | `Error: File not found: ` | | File unreadable | stderr | `Error: Cannot read file: ` | | No argument | stderr | `Usage: bun run validate-yaml ` | **Exit codes**: | Code | Meaning | |------|---------| | 0 | YAML is valid | | 1 | YAML is invalid, file error, or usage error | ### 3.4 Package.json Update Add script entry: ```json "validate-yaml": "bun run src/validate-yaml.ts" ``` ## 4. Technology Stack | Category | Choice | Rationale | |----------|--------|-----------| | Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing project language | | Runtime | Bun | Existing project runtime | | File I/O | `Bun.file().text()` | Bun-native async file reading | | Testing | `bun:test` | Existing test framework | | YAML Parsing | Hand-written syntax validator | No-new-deps constraint (REQ-006); YAML parsing libraries would require adding dependencies | ## 5. Implementation Plan | # | Component | Description | Files | |---|-----------|-------------|-------| | T1 | Core Validation Module | Implement `validateYaml()` function with all syntax checks. Define `ValidationResult` and `ValidationError` types. | `src/yaml-validator.ts` | | T2 | CLI Entry Point | Implement argument parsing, file reading, result output, and exit code logic. | `src/validate-yaml.ts` | | T3 | Unit Tests | Write tests covering valid YAML, each type of syntax error, edge cases (empty file, whitespace-only), and error result structure. | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` | | T4 | Package.json Script | Add `validate-yaml` script entry to package.json. | `package.json` | ## 6. Implementation DAG **Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies): 1. [T1] - Core validation module has no dependencies on other new components 2. [T2, T3] - Both depend on T1 interfaces but are independent of each other 3. [T4] - Script entry references T2's file path **Dependencies**: - T2 -> T1 (Interface: T2 imports `validateYaml` from T1) - T3 -> T1 (Interface: T3 imports `validateYaml` from T1 for testing) - T4 -> T2 (Build: script entry references T2's file path) **Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T4 ## 7. Testing Strategy ### Test Value Assessment | Test Category | Value | Rationale | |---------------|-------|-----------| | Valid YAML acceptance | HIGH | Core business logic -- verifies the tool works for its primary use case | | Invalid YAML detection (each error type) | HIGH | Core business logic -- verifies the tool catches syntax errors | | Error result structure | MEDIUM | Application-specific data contract between validator and CLI | | Edge cases (empty, whitespace-only) | MEDIUM | Application-specific boundary conditions | ### Test Plan (`src/yaml-validator.test.ts`) | Test Group | Test Case | Input | Expected | |------------|-----------|-------|----------| | Valid YAML | Simple key-value | `key: value` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Valid YAML | Nested mapping | Multi-level indented YAML | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Valid YAML | List items | `- item1\n- item2` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Valid YAML | Comments and blank lines | `# comment\n\nkey: value` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Valid YAML | Empty input | `""` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Valid YAML | Flow-style collections | `items: [a, b, c]` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Invalid YAML | Tab indentation | `\tkey: value` | `{ valid: false, errors: [{ line: 1, ... }] }` | | Invalid YAML | Unclosed double quote | `key: "unclosed` | `{ valid: false, errors: [{ line: 1, ... }] }` | | Invalid YAML | Unclosed single quote | `key: 'unclosed` | `{ valid: false, errors: [{ line: 1, ... }] }` | | Invalid YAML | Mismatched brackets | `items: [a, b` | `{ valid: false, errors: [...] }` | | Invalid YAML | Mismatched braces | `obj: {a: 1` | `{ valid: false, errors: [...] }` | | Edge Cases | Whitespace-only | `" \n \n"` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | | Edge Cases | Document markers | `---\nkey: value\n...` | `{ valid: true, errors: [] }` | **Tests NOT included** (low value): - Testing Bun.file() behavior directly (framework behavior) - Testing process.argv parsing (runtime behavior) - Testing console.log/console.error output (library behavior) ## 8. Deployment Design No special deployment steps required. The feature consists of source files added to the existing project structure. **Rollout**: 1. Merge new files into `src/` directory. 2. Update `package.json` with the new script entry. 3. Verify with `bun test` that all tests pass. 4. Command becomes available via `bun run validate-yaml `. **Rollback**: Revert the commit. No database migrations, no infrastructure changes. ## 9. Documentation Impact | Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale | |------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------| | edit | `.rp1/context/modules.md` | Modules | modules.md | Add yaml-validator and validate-yaml as new modules | | edit | `.rp1/context/architecture.md` | Scripts | architecture.md | Add `validate-yaml` to scripts list | | edit | `.rp1/context/index.md` | Project Structure | index.md | Add new files to structure diagram | ## 10. Design Decisions Log See [design-decisions.md](./design-decisions.md) for the full decision log. | ID | Decision | Choice | |----|----------|--------| | D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written syntax validator | | D2 | File structure | Separate entry point + utility module | | D3 | Error reporting format | Structured ValidationResult type | | D4 | File I/O API | Bun.file().text() | | D5 | Script naming | `validate-yaml` |

# Design Decisions: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Created**: 2026-03-08

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written line-by-line syntax validator | No-new-deps constraint (REQ-006) prohibits adding a YAML parsing library. Bun does not include a built-in YAML parser. A hand-written validator targeting common syntax errors is sufficient for the syntax-only scope. | (a) Use `js-yaml` npm package -- rejected due to no-new-deps constraint. (b) Port a subset of a YAML parser -- rejected as overly complex for the scope. (c) Use regex-only validation -- rejected as too fragile for structured syntax. |
| D2 | File structure pattern | Separate CLI entry point (`validate-yaml.ts`) + pure utility module (`yaml-validator.ts`) | Follows existing `index.ts` + `utils.ts` separation pattern. Keeps validation logic testable as pure functions without CLI coupling. | (a) Single file with both CLI and logic -- rejected as inconsistent with existing codebase pattern and harder to test. (b) Add validation to existing `utils.ts` -- rejected as unrelated to existing utils; would bloat that module. |
| D3 | Error reporting format | Structured `ValidationResult` type with `valid` boolean and `errors` array | Provides machine-readable results that the CLI layer can format for human output. Enables testing of specific error details. Follows TypeScript strict mode patterns. | (a) Throw exceptions for invalid YAML -- rejected as validation failures are expected outcomes, not exceptional conditions. (b) Return simple boolean -- rejected as insufficient for error reporting (REQ-003 requires error details). |
| D4 | File I/O API | `Bun.file(path).text()` | Bun-native API, consistent with using the Bun runtime. Returns a promise for async file reading. Throws on missing/unreadable files which aligns with the try/catch error handling pattern. | (a) `node:fs` `readFileSync` -- rejected as synchronous and less idiomatic for Bun. (b) `node:fs/promises` `readFile` -- viable but Bun.file() is more idiomatic. |
| D5 | Script naming | `validate-yaml` | Follows kebab-case naming convention from patterns.md. ## Validation Findings

### HYP-001 Findings
**Validated**: 2026-03-08T15:24:00Z
**Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT
**Result**: CONFIRMED

**Evidence**:

A prototype line-by-line YAML syntax validator was implemented in TypeScript (matching the project language) and tested against a corpus of 69 test cases spanning three test suites:

1. **Baseline suite** (32 cases): Simple key-value, nested mappings, lists, flow sequences/mappings, nested flow collections, block scalar literal `|`, block scalar folded `>`, strip/keep chomping indicators `|-`/`|+`, anchors/aliases, comments, document markers, empty input, whitespace-only, quoted strings with special characters, list of mappings, deep nesting with mixed types, various scalar types, inline comments. Also 9 invalid cases covering tab indentation, unclosed quotes, mismatched brackets/braces. **Result: 32/32 passed (100%).**

2. **Adversarial suite** (23 cases): Multi-line flow sequences/mappings, multi-line plain scalars, colons in unquoted URLs, brackets in unquoted values, block scalars with blank lines, 6-level deep nesting, list of lists, varying indentation amounts, special characters in keys, escape sequences, empty values, compact nested mappings, block scalar termination detection, folded scalar with strip, YAML tags, quoted keys, merge keys with multiple aliases, YAML directives. Also 3 invalid cases. **Result: 22/23 passed (95.7%). 1 false positive: multi-line double-quoted string (A18).**

3. **Edge case suite** (14 cases): Multi-line single-quoted string, explicit newline escapes, quoted brackets in flow context, multiple colons (time format), complex keys with `?` indicator, block scalars with varying indentation, multi-line flow with quotes, aliases as list items, real-world Kubernetes deployment YAML, GitHub Actions workflow YAML, Docker Compose YAML, ESLint config YAML. Also 2 invalid cases. **Result: 13/14 passed (92.9%). 1 false positive: multi-line single-quoted string (E01).**

**Grand total: 67/69 passed (97.1% accuracy, 2.9% failure rate).**

The 2 failures are both false positives (valid YAML incorrectly rejected) caused by the same root issue: **multi-line quoted strings** where a single-quoted or double-quoted string spans multiple lines. A strictly line-by-line parser sees the opening quote on one line and the closing quote on another line, and incorrectly reports unclosed quotes on each line.

Key observations:
- Block scalars (`|`, `>`, `|-`, `>-`, `|+`, `>2`) are handled correctly by tracking block scalar state across lines.
- Multi-line flow collections (`[...\n...]`, `{...\n...}`) are handled correctly by tracking bracket/brace depth across lines.
- All 4 real-world YAML patterns (Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose, ESLint) passed without issue.
- The multi-line quoted string limitation is addressable by adding quote-state tracking across lines (similar to how bracket depth is already tracked), but adds complexity to the "line-by-line" approach.

**Sources**:
- Prototype: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/yaml-validator-prototype.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Baseline tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-corpus.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Adversarial tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-adversarial.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Edge case tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-edge-cases.ts` (DISPOSABLE)

**Implications for Design**:
The line-by-line approach is feasible for the targeted validation scope described in the design document. With a 97.1% accuracy rate across 69 diverse test cases (well below the 10% rejection threshold), the approach handles all common YAML patterns correctly including: nested mappings, flow collections, block scalars with all chomping indicators, anchors/aliases, document markers, and real-world configuration files. The known limitation (multi-line quoted strings) is a rare pattern in typical configuration YAML and can be mitigated by either (a) adding cross-line quote tracking, or (b) documenting it as an unsupported edge case. The design should note this limitation explicitly. The validator does NOT need to be a full spec-compliant parser to be practically useful for catching the most common YAML syntax errors.

## Summary
| Hypothesis | Risk | Result | Implication |
|------------|------|--------|-------------|
| HYP-001: Hand-written line-by-line YAML validator feasibility | HIGH | CONFIRMED | Line-by-line approach achieves 97.1% accuracy across 69 test cases. Known limitation: multi-line quoted strings (2 failures). Feasible for the targeted validation scope with this documented caveat. |

## Code Quality Assessment

**Overall Quality: HIGH**

The implementation demonstrates strong adherence to project patterns and conventions:

1. **File Structure**: The new files (`yaml-validator.ts`, `validate-yaml.ts`, `yaml-validator.test.ts`) follow the established separation pattern of the existing codebase (`utils.ts`, `index.ts`, `utils.test.ts`). The CLI entry point is cleanly separated from the pure validation logic.

2. **Naming Conventions**: All file names are kebab-case, function names are camelCase (`validateYaml`, `checkUnclosedQuotes`, `countFlowIndicators`, `containsUnquotedColon`), and type names are PascalCase (`ValidationResult`, `ValidationError`). This matches the patterns documented in `patterns.md`.

3. **TypeScript Patterns**: Interfaces are properly exported with JSDoc comments. The code uses strict TypeScript conventions with explicit types on function signatures. No use of `any` type.

4. **Error Handling**: The CLI entry point uses a try/catch block with descriptive error messages, consistent with the project's error handling pattern from `patterns.md`.

5. **Testing**: Tests use `bun:test` with `describe`/`test`/`expect` pattern, matching the existing `utils.test.ts` style. Test coverage is comprehensive with 28 tests across 7 describe groups covering valid YAML (10 tests), invalid YAML detection for each error category (10 tests), edge cases (4 tests), and error result structure validation (4 tests).

6. **Module Design**: The `validateYaml()` function is a pure function with no side effects -- it takes a string and returns a `ValidationResult`. The three helper functions (`checkUnclosedQuotes`, `countFlowIndicators`, `containsUnquotedColon`) are properly encapsulated as private module functions.

7. **Code Organization**: The validation logic is well-structured with clear separation of concerns: the main function handles the line-by-line loop and state tracking, while helper functions handle specific syntax checks (quote analysis, flow indicator counting, colon detection).

8. **Known Limitations**: The hypothesis validation documented a 97.1% accuracy rate with a known limitation around multi-line quoted strings. This is a reasonable trade-off for a hand-written validator operating within the no-new-dependencies constraint.

# Requirements Specification: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-03-08

## 1. Feature Overview

The project needs a command-line capability that allows developers to validate YAML files for syntactic correctness directly from the terminal, using only the existing technology stack with no additional dependencies. This provides a lightweight, built-in validation step that can be incorporated into development and CI workflows.

## 2. Business Context

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Developers working with YAML configuration files currently have no built-in way to verify that their YAML is syntactically valid within this project's toolset. Malformed YAML can cause silent failures or confusing errors downstream. A dedicated validation command gives immediate, clear feedback on YAML correctness.

### 2.2 Business Value

- Reduces time spent debugging configuration errors caused by invalid YAML syntax.
- Provides a self-contained validation tool that does not increase the project's dependency footprint.
- Fits naturally into the existing project structure as a reusable utility command.

### 2.3 Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Valid YAML files are correctly accepted | 100% of well-formed YAML input is reported as valid |
| Invalid YAML files produce a clear error | 100% of malformed YAML input results in a descriptive error message |
| No new runtime or dev dependencies introduced | Zero new entries in package.json dependencies or devDependencies (beyond existing) |
| Command is runnable via a single npm/bun script | Accessible via `bun run` script |

## 3. Stakeholders & Users

### 3.1 User Types

| User Type | Description | Relevance |
|-----------|-------------|-----------|
| Developer | A developer using this project who authors or edits YAML files | Primary user; runs the validator to check file correctness |
| CI Pipeline | An automated build/test pipeline | Secondary consumer; may invoke the validator as a pre-check step |

### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests

| Stakeholder | Interest |
|-------------|----------|
| Project Maintainers | Keep the project lean (no new deps); consistent patterns |
| Developers | Fast, clear feedback on YAML validity |

## 4. Scope Definition

### 4.1 In Scope

- Validating YAML files for syntactic correctness (well-formedness).
- Accepting a file path as input.
- Reporting success or failure with a human-readable message.
- Providing a clear, non-zero exit code on validation failure.
- Adding a runnable script entry (e.g., `bun run validate-yaml`).
- Unit tests for the core validation logic.

### 4.2 Out of Scope

- YAML schema validation (e.g., validating against a JSON Schema or custom schema).
- Batch validation of multiple files in a single invocation.
- Auto-fixing or reformatting invalid YAML.
- Support for YAML features beyond standard syntax (e.g., custom tags).
- Interactive or TUI-based validation interface.
- Reading from stdin (may be considered in a future iteration).

### 4.3 Assumptions

- Bun's runtime provides sufficient built-in capabilities to parse YAML without external libraries (or a simple hand-written parser can handle common YAML syntax).
- The YAML files to be validated are of reasonable size (not multi-gigabyte).
- The project will continue using Bun as its runtime.

## 5. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Accept File Path Input
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: Developer
- **Requirement**: The validator command must accept a file path as a command-line argument specifying the YAML file to validate.
- **Rationale**: Developers need to point the tool at a specific file for validation, consistent with how the existing entry point accepts CLI arguments.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: Running the command with a valid file path reads and processes that file.
  - AC-2: Running the command without a file path argument produces a usage message explaining expected input.

### REQ-002: Validate YAML Syntax
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: Developer
- **Requirement**: The command must determine whether the contents of the specified file constitute syntactically valid YAML.
- **Rationale**: This is the core purpose of the feature -- giving developers confidence that their YAML is well-formed.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: A file containing valid YAML produces a success message (e.g., "Valid YAML").
  - AC-2: A file containing invalid YAML (e.g., bad indentation, unclosed quotes, invalid characters) produces an error message describing the problem.

### REQ-003: Report Validation Results Clearly
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: Developer
- **Requirement**: The command must output a clear, human-readable message indicating whether validation succeeded or failed, and in the failure case, include information about what went wrong.
- **Rationale**: Developers need actionable feedback to locate and fix errors in their YAML files.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: On success, a message confirming validity is printed to stdout.
  - AC-2: On failure, an error message is printed to stderr that includes at minimum a description of the syntax error.

### REQ-004: Exit Code Reflects Outcome
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: CI Pipeline
- **Requirement**: The command must exit with code 0 on successful validation and a non-zero exit code on validation failure or error.
- **Rationale**: CI pipelines and scripts rely on exit codes to determine pass/fail status.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: Exit code is 0 when the YAML file is valid.
  - AC-2: Exit code is 1 (or another non-zero value) when the YAML file is invalid.
  - AC-3: Exit code is non-zero when the specified file does not exist or cannot be read.

### REQ-005: Handle Missing or Unreadable Files
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: Developer
- **Requirement**: The command must gracefully handle cases where the specified file does not exist or cannot be read, producing a clear error message.
- **Rationale**: Developers may mistype paths; the tool should fail gracefully rather than crashing with a stack trace.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: If the file does not exist, the command outputs an error message stating the file was not found.
  - AC-2: The command exits with a non-zero exit code when the file is missing or unreadable.

### REQ-006: No New Dependencies
- **Priority**: Must Have
- **User Type**: Project Maintainers
- **Requirement**: The implementation must not introduce any new entries in package.json `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (beyond what already exists).
- **Rationale**: Explicitly stated constraint in the requirements. Keeps the project lean and avoids supply-chain risk.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: The `dependencies` and `devDependencies` fields in package.json remain unchanged (no new packages).

### REQ-007: Runnable via Script Command
- **Priority**: Should Have
- **User Type**: Developer
- **Requirement**: The validator should be runnable via a named script in package.json (e.g., `bun run validate-yaml <filepath>`).
- **Rationale**: Consistent with how the project exposes its existing `dev` and `test` commands; makes discovery easy.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: A script entry exists in package.json that invokes the validator.
  - AC-2: Running the script with a file path argument validates that file.

### REQ-008: Unit Tests for Validation Logic
- **Priority**: Should Have
- **User Type**: Project Maintainers
- **Requirement**: The core validation logic should have unit tests covering valid YAML, invalid YAML, and edge cases.
- **Rationale**: Consistent with the project's existing testing pattern; ensures regression safety.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - AC-1: Tests exist that verify valid YAML input is accepted.
  - AC-2: Tests exist that verify invalid YAML input is rejected with appropriate error information.
  - AC-3: Tests pass when run via `bun test`.

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

### 6.1 Performance Expectations

| Expectation | Target |
|-------------|--------|
| Validation of a typical YAML file (under 1 MB) | Completes in under 1 second |
| Startup overhead | Minimal; no heavy initialization |

### 6.2 Security Requirements

- The command must only read the file specified by the user; it must not write to or modify any files.
- No network access is required or permitted during validation.

### 6.3 Usability Requirements

- Error messages must be understandable to a developer without requiring knowledge of parser internals.
- The command must provide a usage hint when invoked without arguments.

### 6.4 Compliance Requirements

- No additional compliance requirements identified for this feature.

## 7. User Stories

### STORY-001: Validate a YAML Configuration File
- **As a** developer
- **I want to** run a command that checks whether my YAML file is syntactically correct
- **So that** I can catch formatting errors before they cause problems downstream

**Acceptance (GIVEN/WHEN/THEN)**:
- GIVEN a YAML file exists on disk
- WHEN the developer runs the validate-yaml command with that file path
- THEN the command outputs whether the file is valid or invalid, with error details if invalid

### STORY-002: Catch Invalid YAML Early
- **As a** developer
- **I want to** receive a clear error message when my YAML has syntax errors
- **So that** I can quickly locate and fix the problem

**Acceptance (GIVEN/WHEN/THEN)**:
- GIVEN a YAML file with a syntax error (e.g., bad indentation)
- WHEN the developer runs the validate-yaml command
- THEN the output includes a description of the syntax error and the command exits with a non-zero code

### STORY-003: Integrate Validation into CI
- **As a** CI pipeline
- **I want to** invoke the YAML validator and rely on its exit code
- **So that** builds fail automatically when YAML configuration is malformed

**Acceptance (GIVEN/WHEN/THEN)**:
- GIVEN a CI step runs the validate-yaml command against a YAML file
- WHEN the file is invalid
- THEN the command exits with a non-zero code, causing the CI step to fail

### STORY-004: Handle Missing File Gracefully
- **As a** developer
- **I want to** see a helpful error when I provide a wrong file path
- **So that** I know the file was not found rather than seeing a cryptic crash

**Acceptance (GIVEN/WHEN/THEN)**:
- GIVEN no file exists at the specified path
- WHEN the developer runs the validate-yaml command with that path
- THEN the command outputs a "file not found" message and exits with a non-zero code

## 8. Business Rules

| Rule ID | Rule | Rationale |
|---------|------|-----------|
| BR-001 | The validator checks syntax only, not semantic correctness or schema conformance | Keeps scope minimal and achievable without external dependencies |
| BR-002 | No new packages may be added to the project | Explicit constraint from requirements; maintains project simplicity |
| BR-003 | The command follows existing project patterns for CLI arguments and code style | Maintains consistency across the codebase |

## 9. Dependencies & Constraints

| Dependency / Constraint | Type | Impact |
|-------------------------|------|--------|
| Bun runtime | Runtime dependency (existing) | Must use Bun built-in capabilities for YAML parsing |
| No new npm packages | Hard constraint | Validation logic must be implemented using only existing dependencies and built-ins |
| TypeScript strict mode | Convention | All new code must adhere to project TypeScript conventions |
| Co-located tests | Convention | Tests must follow `*.test.ts` pattern next to source files |

## 10. Clarifications Log

| Item | Question | Resolution | Source |
|------|----------|------------|--------|
| CL-001 | What does "simple" mean for the validator? | Minimal, single-purpose command; syntax validation only | Inferred from "simple" + no-new-deps constraint |
| CL-002 | Who are the users? | Developers and CI pipelines | Inferred from project type (utility scripting) |
| CL-003 | Is this a subcommand or standalone script? | Standalone script entry, consistent with existing `src/index.ts` pattern | Inferred from project structure |
| CL-004 | What level of YAML validation? | Syntax/well-formedness only; no schema validation | Conservative inference from "simple" + no-deps constraint |
| CL-005 | What is the input mechanism? | File path via CLI argument | Inferred from existing `process.argv` pattern in index.ts |
| CL-006 | Should it support stdin? | Out of scope for MVP | Conservative scoping decision |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|----------------|--------|-----------|
| PRD selection | No PRD available | No PRD files found in `.rp1/work/prds/`; feature proceeds without parent PRD |

| Script name | `validate-yaml` | Follows kebab-case naming convention from patterns.md |

## AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions

| Actors not specified | Primary: Developer; Secondary: CI pipeline | Inferred from project domain "utility scripting" (KB: concept_map.md) |
| "command" type unclear | New script entry point, similar to existing `src/index.ts` pattern | KB: modules.md, project structure |

# Technical Design: YAML Validator Command **Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command **Version**: 1.0.0 **Created**: 2026-03-08 **Status**: Draft --- ## 1. Design Overview A lightweight CLI command that validates YAML files for syntactic correctness. The command accepts a file path argument, reads the file, runs it through a hand-written YAML syntax validator, and reports the result with appropriate exit codes. No new dependencies are introduced -- all logic is implemented using only Bun built-ins and TypeScript. ### High-Level Architecture ```mermaid graph LR CLI["CLI Entry Point
validate-yaml.ts"] -->|reads| FS["File System
Bun.file()"] CLI -->|calls| VAL["YAML Validator
yaml-validator.ts"] VAL -->|returns| RES["ValidationResult
{valid, errors}"] CLI -->|outputs| OUT["stdout / stderr"] CLI -->|sets| EXIT["process.exit(code)"] TEST["yaml-validator.test.ts"] -->|tests| VAL ``` ## 2. Architecture The feature follows the existing single-layer script architecture. It introduces two new source files that mirror the existing `index.ts` / `utils.ts` separation pattern: a CLI entry point and a pure utility module. ### Component Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "New Files" A["src/validate-yaml.ts
(CLI Entry Point)"] B["src/yaml-validator.ts
(Pure Validation Logic)"] C["src/yaml-validator.test.ts
(Unit Tests)"] end subgraph "Existing Files" D["package.json
(Script Entry)"] end A -->|imports validateYaml| B C -->|imports validateYaml| B D -->|"bun run src/validate-yaml.ts"| A ``` ### Component Descriptions | Component | Purpose | Pattern | |-----------|---------|---------| | `src/yaml-validator.ts` | Pure validation logic. Exports `validateYaml()` function that accepts a string and returns a structured result. | Mirrors `src/utils.ts` -- pure functions, no side effects | | `src/validate-yaml.ts` | CLI entry point. Handles argument parsing, file reading, output formatting, exit codes. | Mirrors `src/index.ts` -- script entry, uses `process.argv` | | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` | Unit tests for the validation function. | Mirrors `src/utils.test.ts` -- co-located, `describe`/`test`/`expect` | | `package.json` (modified) | Adds `validate-yaml` script entry. | Follows existing script naming pattern | ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 Data Model **ValidationResult** -- Return type of the core validation function: ```typescript interface ValidationError { /** 1-based line number where the error was detected */ line: number; /** Human-readable description of the syntax error */ message: string; } interface ValidationResult { /** Whether the YAML content is syntactically valid */ valid: boolean; /** List of syntax errors found (empty if valid) */ errors: ValidationError[]; } ``` ### 3.2 Core Validation Logic (`src/yaml-validator.ts`) **Exported function**: ```typescript export function validateYaml(content: string): ValidationResult ``` **Validation checks performed** (in order): | Check | Description | Example Invalid Input | |-------|-------------|----------------------| | Tab indentation | YAML spec forbids tabs for indentation | `\tkey: value` | | Unclosed quoted strings | Detect unmatched single or double quotes in scalar values | `key: "unclosed value` | | Mismatched flow indicators | Unbalanced `[]` or `{}` in flow-style collections | `items: [a, b, c` | | Invalid mapping syntax | Lines that appear to be key-value pairs but have structural issues | `key value` (missing colon separator) | | Inconsistent indentation | Child items with indentation that does not align to a consistent block level | Mixed 2-space and 3-space nesting | | Document marker validation | Ensure `---` and `...` document markers are used correctly | `-- -` (malformed marker) | **Design notes**: - The validator processes the input line-by-line for simplicity and clarity. - Comment lines (starting with `#` after optional whitespace) and blank lines are skipped. - The validator does NOT attempt full YAML spec compliance. It targets common, practical syntax errors that developers encounter. - Empty input and whitespace-only input are treated as valid (empty YAML document). ### 3.3 CLI Entry Point (`src/validate-yaml.ts`) **Flow**: ```mermaid graph TB START["Start"] --> ARGS["Read process.argv[2]"] ARGS -->|missing| USAGE["Print usage to stderr
Exit code 1"] ARGS -->|present| READ["Read file via Bun.file(path).text()"] READ -->|error| FILEERR["Print file error to stderr
Exit code 1"] READ -->|success| VALIDATE["Call validateYaml(content)"] VALIDATE -->|valid| SUCCESS["Print success to stdout
Exit code 0"] VALIDATE -->|invalid| FAIL["Print errors to stderr
Exit code 1"] ``` **Output format**: | Scenario | Stream | Message | |----------|--------|---------| | Valid YAML | stdout | `Valid YAML: ` | | Invalid YAML | stderr | `Invalid YAML: \n Line : ` (one line per error) | | File not found | stderr | `Error: File not found: ` | | File unreadable | stderr | `Error: Cannot read file: ` | | No argument | stderr | `Usage: bun run validate-yaml ` | **Exit codes**: | Code | Meaning | |------|---------| | 0 | YAML is valid | | 1 | YAML is invalid, file error, or usage error | ### 3.4 Package.json Update Add script entry: ```json "validate-yaml": "bun run src/validate-yaml.ts" ``` ## 4. Technology Stack | Category | Choice | Rationale | |----------|--------|-----------| | Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing project language | | Runtime | Bun | Existing project runtime | | File I/O | `Bun.file().text()` | Bun-native async file reading | | Testing | `bun:test` | Existing test framework | | YAML Parsing | Hand-written syntax validator | No-new-deps constraint (REQ-006); YAML parsing libraries would require adding dependencies | ## 5. ## Decision Log

| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written line-by-line syntax validator | No-new-deps constraint (REQ-006) prohibits adding a YAML parsing library. Bun does not include a built-in YAML parser. A hand-written validator targeting common syntax errors is sufficient for the syntax-only scope. | (a) Use `js-yaml` npm package -- rejected due to no-new-deps constraint. (b) Port a subset of a YAML parser -- rejected as overly complex for the scope. (c) Use regex-only validation -- rejected as too fragile for structured syntax. |
| D2 | File structure pattern | Separate CLI entry point (`validate-yaml.ts`) + pure utility module (`yaml-validator.ts`) | Follows existing `index.ts` + `utils.ts` separation pattern. Keeps validation logic testable as pure functions without CLI coupling. | (a) Single file with both CLI and logic -- rejected as inconsistent with existing codebase pattern and harder to test. (b) Add validation to existing `utils.ts` -- rejected as unrelated to existing utils; would bloat that module. |
| D3 | Error reporting format | Structured `ValidationResult` type with `valid` boolean and `errors` array | Provides machine-readable results that the CLI layer can format for human output. Enables testing of specific error details. Follows TypeScript strict mode patterns. | (a) Throw exceptions for invalid YAML -- rejected as validation failures are expected outcomes, not exceptional conditions. (b) Return simple boolean -- rejected as insufficient for error reporting (REQ-003 requires error details). |
| D4 | File I/O API | `Bun.file(path).text()` | Bun-native API, consistent with using the Bun runtime. Returns a promise for async file reading. Throws on missing/unreadable files which aligns with the try/catch error handling pattern. | (a) `node:fs` `readFileSync` -- rejected as synchronous and less idiomatic for Bun. (b) `node:fs/promises` `readFile` -- viable but Bun.file() is more idiomatic. |
| D5 | Script naming | `validate-yaml` | Follows kebab-case naming convention from patterns.md. Descriptive and consistent with existing script names (`dev`, `test`, `lint`, `format`). | (a) `yaml-validate` -- rejected as less natural English phrasing. (b) `check-yaml` -- viable but "validate" more precisely describes the action. |
| D6 | Test co-location | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` alongside `src/yaml-validator.ts` | Follows existing pattern where `utils.test.ts` is co-located with `utils.ts`. Consistent with patterns.md and tsconfig.json include paths. | (a) Separate `tests/` directory -- rejected as inconsistent with existing codebase pattern. |
| D7 | Exit code scheme | 0 for valid, 1 for all errors (invalid YAML, missing file, usage error) | Simple and standard. Consistent with Unix conventions. CI pipelines only need zero vs non-zero distinction. | (a) Different codes per error type (1=invalid, 2=file error, 3=usage) -- rejected as over-engineering for this scope; no requirement distinguishes error types by exit code. |

## Validation Findings

### HYP-001 Findings
**Validated**: 2026-03-08T15:24:00Z
**Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT
**Result**: CONFIRMED

**Evidence**:

A prototype line-by-line YAML syntax validator was implemented in TypeScript (matching the project language) and tested against a corpus of 69 test cases spanning three test suites:

1. **Baseline suite** (32 cases): Simple key-value, nested mappings, lists, flow sequences/mappings, nested flow collections, block scalar literal `|`, block scalar folded `>`, strip/keep chomping indicators `|-`/`|+`, anchors/aliases, comments, document markers, empty input, whitespace-only, quoted strings with special characters, list of mappings, deep nesting with mixed types, various scalar types, inline comments. Also 9 invalid cases covering tab indentation, unclosed quotes, mismatched brackets/braces. **Result: 32/32 passed (100%).**

2. **Adversarial suite** (23 cases): Multi-line flow sequences/mappings, multi-line plain scalars, colons in unquoted URLs, brackets in unquoted values, block scalars with blank lines, 6-level deep nesting, list of lists, varying indentation amounts, special characters in keys, escape sequences, empty values, compact nested mappings, block scalar termination detection, folded scalar with strip, YAML tags, quoted keys, merge keys with multiple aliases, YAML directives. Also 3 invalid cases. **Result: 22/23 passed (95.7%). 1 false positive: multi-line double-quoted string (A18).**

3. **Edge case suite** (14 cases): Multi-line single-quoted string, explicit newline escapes, quoted brackets in flow context, multiple colons (time format), complex keys with `?` indicator, block scalars with varying indentation, multi-line flow with quotes, aliases as list items, real-world Kubernetes deployment YAML, GitHub Actions workflow YAML, Docker Compose YAML, ESLint config YAML. Also 2 invalid cases. **Result: 13/14 passed (92.9%). 1 false positive: multi-line single-quoted string (E01).**

**Grand total: 67/69 passed (97.1% accuracy, 2.9% failure rate).**

The 2 failures are both false positives (valid YAML incorrectly rejected) caused by the same root issue: **multi-line quoted strings** where a single-quoted or double-quoted string spans multiple lines. A strictly line-by-line parser sees the opening quote on one line and the closing quote on another line, and incorrectly reports unclosed quotes on each line.

Key observations:
- Block scalars (`|`, `>`, `|-`, `>-`, `|+`, `>2`) are handled correctly by tracking block scalar state across lines.
- Multi-line flow collections (`[...\n...]`, `{...\n...}`) are handled correctly by tracking bracket/brace depth across lines.
- All 4 real-world YAML patterns (Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose, ESLint) passed without issue.
- The multi-line quoted string limitation is addressable by adding quote-state tracking across lines (similar to how bracket depth is already tracked), but adds complexity to the "line-by-line" approach.

**Sources**:
- Prototype: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/yaml-validator-prototype.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Baseline tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-corpus.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Adversarial tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-adversarial.ts` (DISPOSABLE)
- Edge case tests: `/tmp/hypothesis-yaml-validator-command/test-edge-cases.ts` (DISPOSABLE)

**Implications for Design**:
The line-by-line approach is feasible for the targeted validation scope described in the design document. With a 97.1% accuracy rate across 69 diverse test cases (well below the 10% rejection threshold), the approach handles all common YAML patterns correctly including: nested mappings, flow collections, block scalars with all chomping indicators, anchors/aliases, document markers, and real-world configuration files. The known limitation (multi-line quoted strings) is a rare pattern in typical configuration YAML and can be mitigated by either (a) adding cross-line quote tracking, or (b) documenting it as an unsupported edge case. The design should note this limitation explicitly. The validator does NOT need to be a full spec-compliant parser to be practically useful for catching the most common YAML syntax errors.

## Summary
| Hypothesis | Risk | Result | Implication |
|------------|------|--------|-------------|
| HYP-001: Hand-written line-by-line YAML validator feasibility | HIGH | CONFIRMED | Line-by-line approach achieves 97.1% accuracy across 69 test cases. Known limitation: multi-line quoted strings (2 failures). Feasible for the targeted validation scope with this documented caveat. |
